metaDesc: A guide to desserts, bakeries and dessert cafes in Trang, Thailand — from the original Trang sponge cake to Soi 9 mooncakes, plus Thai-sweets cafes and homemade bakeries with neighborhoods, prices and real opening hours.

h1:
Desserts, Bakeries & Dessert Cafes
in Trang Town
intro: Trang is famous for its roast pork and dim sum, but the dessert side of town is just as good. You'll find original sponge cakes that have been around for decades, mooncakes everyone takes home as gifts, and a new wave of Thai-sweets cafes and homemade bakeries where you can sit and chill all afternoon. We've picked 10 spots that Trang locals actually go to, with the neighborhood, prices and the best time to visit for each.

blocks.html: Trang's desserts split easily into three lanes. There's the classic take-home stuff like Trang sponge cake and mooncakes you can carry back as gifts; the old-school Thai sweets that get harder to find every year; and the new-wave cafes that serve Thai sweets and bakery items in a nice room. We've ordered the list with the things that are most distinctly Trang first, then worked our way down to the sit-and-relax spots.

blocks.text: 10 desserts and shops you have to try

items.name: Trang Sponge Cake (Tha Pap Cake)
items.blurb: Trang sponge cake is the province's signature dessert, adapted from the egg cake of the Hainanese Chinese. It's soft, fragrant with pandan and just sweet enough. Tha Pap is the famous name that most people take home as a gift, and its standout is the young coconut cake with fresh coconut flesh baked right into the sponge. The shop sits on Trang-Phatthalung Road and is easy to spot in pink.

items.name: Khuk Ming Cake (Lamphura)
items.blurb: An original cake that's been part of Trang for over 80 years. It's an old-style sponge with a texture close to egg cake, a hole in the middle, no cream topping, no baking powder and no preservatives. If you genuinely like cake the traditional way, this is the one. It's out in Lamphura, Huai Yot district — a bit of a drive past town, but worth it.

items.name: Soi 9 Mooncakes
items.blurb: The gift people say you haven't really been to Trang without stopping for. This shop has been going for more than 40 years — thin pastry, crisp outside and soft inside. The best-selling filling is taro with salted egg yolk, made with Trang's large duck eggs. There are plenty of fillings too: red bean, durian, green tea and purple yam. It's on Soi 9 off Huai Yot Road, right in the center of town.
items.meta: Soi 9, Huai Yot Rd · town center

items.name: Hnom Whan Home Cafe
items.blurb: A Thai-sweets cafe from the Je Mong dessert family, with its strength in the sheer variety of Thai sweets that cost just a few tens of baht each — khanom piak poon, sago, and pung kem among them. It's done up in a vintage English-garden style with lots of photo corners, and you can sit in the air-conditioned room or outside. A good place to take an afternoon break.

items.name: Laau Cafe
items.blurb: A small homemade cafe in town that bakery fans will love, because they make their bread from natural yeast — sourdough, scones, cookies, carrot cake and brownies, all to pair with coffee. The shop is little but the lineup is solid. It's on Charoenchit Road near a 7-Eleven, so it's easy to find.

items.name: Green House Na Trang
items.blurb: A home-bake cake shop that runs on a home-baked-and-heart-made approach, baking fresh day by day. The focus is on cake slices and baked goods to go with a drink, and it suits anyone who likes homey, not-too-sweet bakery-style cake. It's a comfortable place to sit, open Tuesday through Sunday.

items.name: Manila Cafe
items.blurb: A cafe in an old wooden house with a retro feel, on Soi Khao Pae Choi across from Tessaban Wat Tantayaram School. The draw is that it serves both Thai sweets and bakery items under one roof, alongside a long drinks menu. Good for anyone who wants the quiet, wooden-house atmosphere.
items.meta: Soi Khao Pae Choi · in town

items.name: Gray 18 Cafe
items.blurb: A cafe done up in a raw, pared-back style in town, good for getting work done or meeting friends. The menu has coffee, tea and sweets to choose from, with easygoing starting prices. It's a place Trang locals drop by regularly when they want a relaxed seat that isn't crowded.

items.name: Jirawan Old-Style Salty-Sweet Cake (Huai Yot)
items.blurb: A hard-to-find Trang sweet that brings sweet and salty together in one bite, from a recipe that's a century old. It's made in Huai Yot by this one shop only. If you like trying unusual, traditional things that the younger generation rarely comes across anymore, this is the real off-the-radar find.
items.meta: Huai Yot · a drive past town

items.name: Local Sweets at the Fresh Market
items.blurb: If you want Thai-Trang sweets at everyday-local prices, the in-town fresh market in the morning has it all — khanom chak, khanom tian, fluffy khanom thuay fu and khanom chan, with the vendors rotating by the day. It's made fresh that morning, so grab some before you walk the market.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Trang sponge cake is a fresh cake with no preservatives, so if you're buying it as a gift, eat it within 2–3 days and keep it in the fridge. Mooncakes last longer and are the better pick if you're carrying them a long way.

blocks.text: Trang sponge cake, the province's signature dessert

blocks.html: If you had to pick one dessert to represent Trang, a lot of people would think of Trang sponge cake first. It started from the egg cake of the Hainanese Chinese who migrated to Trang, and was gradually adjusted into the soft, pandan-scented cake we know today. The legendary original is Khuk Ming cake out in Lamphura, while the name most people buy as a gift in town is Tha Pap.

items: Young coconut cake — fresh coconut flesh baked into the sponge; it's Tha Pap's best seller.
Pandan / butter cake — the basic recipes, fragrant and not too sweet, great with coffee.
Khuk Ming hole-in-the-middle cake — the truly traditional style, no topping, with a texture close to egg cake.

blocks.text: Dessert cafes and bakeries in town

blocks.html: Lately Trang has seen a lot more dessert cafes open up, from Thai-sweets shops dressed up in cute decor like Hnom Whan Home Cafe to homemade bakeries like Laau that bake their own natural-yeast bread. On a day when you've eaten your fill of savory food, look for one of these places to take an afternoon break — have a sweet, sip a coffee, then carry on.

items.name: For Thai sweets
items.blurb: Hnom Whan Home Cafe and Manila Cafe serve Thai sweets in a cafe setting at easygoing prices — good for anyone who likes homey desserts.

items.name: For bakery
items.blurb: Laau and Green House focus on homemade baked goods — sourdough, scones, cake slices — not too sweet and great with black coffee.

blocks.text: What to buy as a gift

blocks.html: If you're set on carrying something home, Soi 9 mooncakes are the safest choice because they keep well and travel easily. Trang sponge cake works if you'll eat it within a few days. You can buy both in town, so there's no need to drive far.

faq.a: Trang sponge cake is the province's signature dessert — a soft, pandan-scented cake adapted from the egg cake of the Hainanese Chinese. Next come Soi 9 mooncakes, which people love to buy as gifts, and the local Thai sweets you'll find at the morning markets.

faq.q: Where's the best place to buy Trang sponge cake?
faq.a: The legendary original is Khuk Ming cake in Lamphura, Huai Yot district, open 06:00–19:00. The name most people buy as a gift in town is Tha Pap, on Trang-Phatthalung Road, open 07:00–18:00 and closed Wednesdays.

faq.q: Which Soi 9 mooncake filling is the best?
faq.a: The best-selling filling is taro with salted egg yolk, made with Trang's large duck eggs — thin pastry, crisp outside and soft inside. A box of 10 is 120 baht. There are also red bean, durian, green tea and purple yam fillings to choose from.

faq.q: Can you work from the dessert cafes in Trang?
faq.a: Yes. A place like Gray 18 Cafe has a pared-back style that's good for working, while Hnom Whan Home Cafe has both an air-conditioned zone and outdoor seating that's comfortable in the afternoon. Drinks start at around 40–50 baht.

faq.q: How long do Trang desserts keep?
faq.a: Trang sponge cake is a fresh cake with no preservatives, so eat it within 2–3 days and keep it in the fridge. Mooncakes last quite a few days longer and are the better pick if you're carrying them far.
